html:
The Akawaio are a Carib-speaking people of the upper Mazaruni basin in western Guyana, with smaller communities in Venezuela and Brazil. They call themselves Kapon, a name they share with the closely related Patamona.

They live in forest and savanna villages near the Pakaraima Mountains, growing cassava, hunting and fishing. For centuries they traded with the Dutch on the coast and with peoples further inland, such as the Macuxi and Pemon. In the 1800s a religious movement called Hallelujah, which blends Christian and native ideas, spread among them and is still practised. Gold and diamond mining in the Mazaruni has long pressed on their land in Guyana, once British Guiana.
